impDef.description: Whether the Java interface java.io.Serializable or the Java interface java.sql.SQLData will be used for object state conversion in those cases where the user-defined type definition does not specify an interface specification.

Whether a Java method called by an SQL name executes with “definer’s rights” or “invoker’s rights” — that is, whether it executes with the user-name of the user who performed the SQL-invoked routine or the user-name of the current user.
Whether the validation of the Java parameter declaration list is to be performed by routine invocation, or not.
The effect of invoking an external Java routine when the JDBC connection object that created any element of the result set parameters is closed.
The effect of invoking an external Java routine when any element of the result set parameters is not an object returned by a connection to the current SQL system and SQL session.
Whether an external Java routine returns update counts as defined in JDBC.

Whether validation of the explicit or implicit Java parameter declaration list of an external Java data type is performed by user-defined type definition or when the corresponding SQL-invoked method is invoked.
The rules to which an SQLJ.INSTALL_JAR procedure is subject for executing SQL-schema statements within SQL-transactions.
The effect on the install actions when an invocation of SQLJ.INSTALL_JAR raises an exception condition.
The rules used to determine if the values and format of a url parameter are valid for SQLJ.INSTALL_JAR.
The rules to which an SQLJ.REPLACE_JAR procedure is subject for executing SQL-schema statements within SQL-transactions.
The rules used to determine if the values and format of a url parameter are valid for SQLJ.REPLACE_JAR.
The rules to which an SQLJ.REMOVE_JAR procedure is subject for executing SQL-schema statements within SQL-transactions.
The effect on the remove actions when an invocation of SQLJ.REMOVE_JAR raises an exception condition.
The rules to which an SQLJ.ALTER_JAVA_PATH procedure is subject for executing SQL-schema statements within SQL-transactions.
The effect on the remove actions when an invocation of SQLJ.ALTER_JAVA_PATH raises an exception condition.
The data source URLs that are supported by java.sql in addition to the default connection.

Whether an implementer block with a given implementer name is interpreted as an install action or remove action, i.e., an SQL/JRT implementation may (but is not required to) perform install or remove actions specified by some other SQL/JRT implementation.
The interface using clause of an external Java type when not explicitly specified.
The Java packages, other than java.sql, supplied by SQL systems that implement ISO/IEC 9075-13.
The maximum length of a url, jar or path.
The maximum lengths of the package identifier, class identifier, Java field name, and Java method name.
The maximum number of returned result sets that may be returned by an SQL-invoked routine.
The specification of the implementer block, if any, provided in a deployment descriptor file to allow specification of custom install and remove actions.
The length for an SQL parameter declaration whose data type is character string.
The length of a java.lang.StringBuffer used as a save area data item.
The implementer names, which are SQL identifier, that are specified in an implementer block.
The character set supported for ‹package identifier›, ‹class identifier›, ‹Java field name›, and ‹Java method name›.
The result value of an output parameter with the data type of the declared data type of the parameter when the subject routine is an external Java routine.
The privileges required to invoke the SQLJ.INSTALL_JAR, SQLJ.REPLACE_JAR, and SQLJ.REMOVE_JAR procedures.
The method of execution of a subject Java class’s implementation of writeObject() to convert a Java value to an SQL value.
The method of execution of a subject Java class’s implementation of writeSQL() to convert a Java value to an SQL value.
The method of execution of a subject Java class’s implementation of readObject() to convert an SQL value to a Java object.
The method of execution of a subject Java class’s implementation of readSQL() to convert an SQL value to a Java object.
The mechanism used to invoke a constructor of an external Java data type when Feature J571, “NEW operator”, is not supported.
The privileges required to invoke the SQLJ.INSTALL_JAR procedure.
The privileges required to invoke the SQLJ.REPLACE_JAR procedure.
The privileges required to invoke the SQLJ.REMOVE_JAR procedure.
The privileges required to invoke the SQLJ.ALTER_JAVA_PATH procedure.
